title: fix: back off and give up on repeated render submit failures
body:
Closes #2688

## Problem

When the kernel rejects every atomic commit for an output, the redraw timer in `queue_redraw` re-queues a
forced redraw immediately after each failure, with no delay and no limit. smithay logs
`New screen configuration invalid!` with the full `AtomicRequest` dump on every attempt, so the loop
floods the journal (in #2688 it filled 158 GiB of disk in 18.5 h) and keeps the compositor busy.

The dead output's `DrmCompositor` also stays registered with the `DrmOutputManager`. `use_mode`,
`initialize_output` and `allow_primary_scanout_any` submit on every registered compositor, so
output-configuration requests for the *other* outputs fail as well, and the first
`cosmic-randr disable` of the dead output is rejected (`Failed to switch primary-plane scanout flags`).

## Change

In the surface thread (`src/backend/kms/surface/mod.rs`, first commit) and the DPMS handler
(`src/wayland/handlers/output_power.rs`, second commit):

- A redraw that fails before KMS takes the frame retries after an exponential back-off: one frame
  time, doubling, capped at 4 s. Redraw requests during the back-off wait for it.
- After 12 consecutive failures, if the error chain contains a `DrmError` (KMS rejected the frame),
  the surface stops rendering and deactivates the same way a session pause does (`active = false`,
  `DrmOutput` dropped). The next `apply_config_for_outputs` then disables or re-initializes it; that
  also happens on VT switch / session resume and on a DRM udev change.
- Other errors (e.g. no renderer after a GPU reset) keep retrying at the cap and never give up, since
  they clear by themselves.
- The failure count resets on the first frame KMS accepts, on resume, and on DPMS off.
- When outputs are powered on (input or wlr-output-power) and a woken surface has given up, the
  output config is re-applied once on idle (`refresh_output_config()`, as on a DRM udev change), so a
  later wake can still bring the output back. The old loop recovered that way: on the rig below, 2 of
  6 stuck episodes on the stock build healed by themselves at a later wake (2 of 8 wakes while stuck).
- Logging is per state change: first failure (warn), giving up (error), recovery and
  re-initialization (warn, so the episode is closed at the default log level).

Out of scope: why the commit is rejected in the first place, and smithay logging the whole atomic
request at warn level. Known limitation, shared with session resume and hotplug:
`apply_config_for_outputs` stops at the first output that fails to initialize, so if two outputs gave
up and one still fails at wake, the other is not re-initialized either. And while a given-up output
stays enabled in the config, a request that keeps it enabled (e.g. any change from the display
settings) retries it and is rejected if the kernel still refuses; disabling it is accepted. Marking
such an output disabled in the config would avoid that, but is a policy change left for a follow-up.

## Testing

Fedora 44, NVIDIA GTX 1060 on 580.178.04, three outputs (DP-1 3840x2160@120, DP-3 and HDMI-A-1
2560x1440@100). One output intermittently fails to come back after the screens sleep (HDMI-A-1
on 6 of 18 wakes from a healthy state between 2026-09-25 and 2026-10-02 on the stock build; DP-3 in
the patched run below), with the same `Atomic Test failed for new properties on crtc` /
`Error setting crtc ... Invalid argument` errors as #2688.

| | stock 1.8.0 | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| render failures after the wake | 1,300-3,500/s (logged + journald-suppressed), unbounded | 11 attempts in 14 s, then gives up |
| cosmic-comp log lines of its own | one per attempt | 2 (first failure, giving up) |
| cosmic-comp CPU | ~110% | ~13% (idle) |
| `cosmic-randr list` / kernel for the dead output | enabled / disabled | enabled / disabled until reconfigured |
| `cosmic-randr disable <dead output>` | 1st rejected, 2nd accepted | 1st accepted |
| re-enabling it afterwards (mode change script) | works after the 2nd disable | works, no log-out |

The re-apply on wake, on device, twice: after a system suspend/resume the session-resume reload could
not re-initialize DP-3 (`Invalid argument` from the kernel), which leaves the output dark on the stock
build too; and HDMI-A-1 gave up 14 s after a natural wake. In both cases the next DPMS off/on
re-applied the config and the output came back with no manual steps.

`cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` (default and `debug` features),
`cargo check --no-default-features` and `cargo test` pass; `--all-features` (tracy) was not built
locally. Unit tests cover the back-off sequence and the KMS-rejection classification.
